items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law and the insurance law, in relation to credits for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6369

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the tax law and the insurance law, in relation to
credits for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :

The purpose of this bill is to expand upon the provisions of Chapter
563 of the Laws of 2010 and Chapter 465 of the Laws of 2014, which
expanded the types of end of life care that can be financed by an
accelerated death benefit rider attached to a life insurance policy.
Under these new laws, persons who have resided in a nursing home for
three months or more or require end of life or palliative care for
three months or more at a residential, health care facility, receive
home care services or hospice care and such services are expected to
be needed until death can now be financed by a life insurance policy
rider. This bill expands the current tax credit inducements that exist
for the purchase of long term care insurance to also include these new
life insurance policy riders.

A similar bill S. 5230-A / A. 7607-A (Klein / Gjonaj)passed both the
Assembly and Senate in 2015, but it was vetoed due to certain
suggested technical deficiencies and cross references that may need to
have been included in the bill.This bill adds a new bill section 5
that amends Insurance Law section 1117 to add those cross references
to ensure that the Superintendent must approval of all long term care
policy riders that are eligible for a tax credit.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Amends Tax Law section 190 to extend the tax credit for
purchasing long term care insurance (20% of the premium paid) to
include a policy rider to a life insurance policy that provides for
long term care-like coverages. The reason for this expansion is
because, under new laws recently adopted in New York, the life
insurance rider can now pay for accelerated benefits for end of life
care that covers the same types of end of life care covered under long
term care insurance.

Section 2: Amends Tax Law section 210-B to expand the tax credit
incen- tives currently used to encourage the purchase long term care
insurance (20% of the premium paid)to include premiums paid to
purchase life insurance riders that cover similar end of life expenses
as it relates to the corporate franchise rate.

Section 3: Amends Tax Law section 606 to add the LTC (long term care)
life insurance policy rider premiums paid that is eligible for a tax
credit, in addition the tax credit that is currently available for
long term care insurance for personnel income tax calculations.

Section 4: Amends Tax Law section 1511 to add the LTC tax credit for
the purchase of life insurance policy riders for insurance corporation
taxes.

Section 5: Amends Insurance Law section 1117 (g) to make a technical
amendment to cross reference and ensure that the Superintendent of
Financial Services approves all life insurance policy riders that are
eligible to obtain an income tax credit, as is currently the case for
free standing long term care insurance policies.

 JUSTIFICATION :

As the general population becomes older, more and more individuals are
looking for affordable ways to finance their nursing home and long
term care needs. While there are available policies that provide
payment for long term care, more products should be authorized under
New York law so that consumers will have more types of insurance
coverage available to meet their specific needs or the needs of their
family. This can be done by encouraging more younger persons to obtain
such coverage and incentivize more life insurers to offer such
coverages. By both encouraging persons to purchase such policies and
incentivizing carriers to offer such policy riders, this should
greatly expand the number of covered lives protected.

In addition, encouraging more individuals to finance their own long
term care, will help to curtail future expenditures from the State's
Medicaid program, which currently finances the lion's share of the
provision of long term care in this State. This bill is a further
extension of new laws such as Chapter 563 of the Laws of 2010 and
Chapter 465 of the Laws of 2014 which are geared towards encouraging
individuals to finance their own long term care and nursing home care
as we all get older via life insurance policy riders.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill, that has been introduced to include technical changes to S.
5230-A / A. 7607-A, that was vetoed, for certain technical cross
references in the law that may have been needed.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

It is the intent of this bill encourage the increased use: of Long
Term Care insurance and policy riders to life insurance policies for
the use as a financing mechanism to finance end of life care. This, in
the end, should help to decrease State Medicaid expenditures.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on April, 1st of the year next succeeding
its date of enactment.

summary: Establishes tax credits for premiums paid for life insurance which is used for long term health care.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 303

TO THE SENATE:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:

Senate Bill Number 6369 entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to amend the tax law and the insurance law, in relation to
      credits for premiums paid for long-term care insurance policies"

    NOT APPROVED

  This bill would extend the long-term  care  insurance  tax  credit  to
include a 20% credit for any premiums paid toward a life insurance poli-
cy that has an accelerated death benefit rider.

  For many individuals, long-term care insurance is a critical financial
tool  to  ensure  adequate  coverage for long-term personal or custodial
care. My Administration has taken substantial steps to support  individ-
uals  in  need  of long term care, including the Department of Financial
Services' collaborative efforts to work with consumers and the insurance
industry to establish standards for long term care  insurance  products.
More  recently, additional funding was allocated to the State's Expanded
In-Home Services for the Elderly  Program,  a  partnership  between  the
state  and  the counties to provide non-medical services and support for
seniors who require help with basic daily activities.

  I continue to support the need to  provide  additional  assistance  to
individuals  in  need of long term care. However, this bill suffers from
the same fundamental flaw as the bill I vetoed last year (Veto  No.  268
of  2015)  --  it  does  not  identify a designated source of funding to
offset the significant cost of providing a tax credit for premiums  paid
for  long-term  care  insurance  policies. Such funding decisions should
occur in the context of the annual budget negotiations.

  Thus, while I am constrained to veto this bill,  I  am  directing  the
Department  of  Financial  Services to work with the bill's sponsors and
interested stakeholders to develop recommendations to address the impor-
tant policy goals advanced by this legislation in a fiscally responsible
manner.

  This bill is disapproved.                   (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
